subject: Mathematics

sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: CONNECTING THE DOTS… 5 5.1 Of Questions and Statements Your teacher tells you that they are meeting two of their childhood friends this evening.
sections.source_evidence: CONNECTING THE DOTS… 5 5.1 Of Questions and Statements Your teacher tells you that they are meeting two of their childhood friends this evening.

sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: One is 5 feet tall and the other is 6 feet tall.
sections.source_evidence: One is 5 feet tall and the other is 6 feet tall.

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: What is your guess as to each friend’s gender based on this information?
sections.source_evidence: What is your guess as to each friend’s gender based on this information?

sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: You might have guessed that the 5-foot-tall person is a woman and the 6-foot-tall person is a man.
sections.source_evidence: You might have guessed that the 5-foot-tall person is a woman and the 6-foot-tall person is a man.

sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: But experience tells us that 5-foot-tall men and 6-foot-tall women are rare.
sections.source_evidence: But experience tells us that 5-foot-tall men and 6-foot-tall women are rare.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: We have seen that, more often, men are taller than women.
sections.source_evidence: We have seen that, more often, men are taller than women.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: The above is a simple example of statistical thinking.
sections.source_evidence: The above is a simple example of statistical thinking.

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: We regularly come across statements like — Jemimah’s batting has been very consistent over the past year.
sections.source_evidence: We regularly come across statements like — Jemimah’s batting has been very consistent over the past year.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: We can expect a century from her in tomorrow’s match.
sections.source_evidence: We can expect a century from her in tomorrow’s match.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: I take about 15 minutes to cycle from school to home.
sections.source_evidence: I take about 15 minutes to cycle from school to home.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: I think my pen might last for 2 more weeks; it is time to get a new one soon.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: The population of their village has reduced by about 100 in the last decade.
sections.source_evidence: The population of their village has reduced by about 100 in the last decade.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: Since I started to eat fruits and vegetables more frequently, I am able to run 2 km more each day.
sections.source_evidence: Since I started to eat fruits and vegetables more frequently, I am able to run 2 km more each day.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: David spends about 7 hours daily in the school.

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: Ganita Prakash | Grade 7 | Part-II We call these statistical statements.
sections.source_evidence: Ganita Prakash | Grade 7 | Part-II We call these statistical statements.

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: Simply put, a statistical statement is a claim or summary about some phenomenon, expressed in terms of numerical values, proportions, probabilities, or predictions.
sections.source_evidence: Simply put, a statistical statement is a claim or summary about some phenomenon, expressed in terms of numerical values, proportions, probabilities, or predictions.

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: A statistical question is a question that can be answered by collecting data.
sections.source_evidence: A statistical question is a question that can be answered by collecting data.

sections.heading: Learning Point 18
sections.content: For example, “How tall are Grade 7 students in our school?” is a statistical question.
sections.source_evidence: For example, “How tall are Grade 7 students in our school?” is a statistical question.

sections.heading: Learning Point 19
sections.content: We expect that not all Grade 7 students have the same height, but we can collect data, analyse it, and make conclusions about the heights that do occur.
sections.source_evidence: We expect that not all Grade 7 students have the same height, but we can collect data, analyse it, and make conclusions about the heights that do occur.

sections.heading: Learning Point 20
sections.content: The question “Typically, are onions costlier in Yahapur or Wahapur?” is also a statistical question.
sections.source_evidence: The question “Typically, are onions costlier in Yahapur or Wahapur?” is also a statistical question.
